chunks: And by this chain, Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) said:
Do not reckon those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive, receiving provision from their Lord.

And I testify that Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), the Messenger of Allah, died as a martyr. By Allah, he will surely come to you, so be certain when he comes to you, for Shayṭān cannot take on his likeness.

Then ʿAlī took Abū Bakr by the hand and showed him the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله). So he said to him: O Abū Bakr, believe in ʿAlī and in eleven of his descendants. They are like me except for prophethood. And repent to Allah from that which is in your hand, for you have no right in it.
He said: Then he went away and was not seen.

key_terms.آمِنْ: believe; a command here to affirm ʿAlī and the eleven from his descendants
key_terms.أَحْيَاءٌ: alive; indicating continued life and provision with their Lord
key_terms.النُّبُوَّةَ: prophethood; the one distinction excluded from the likeness mentioned
key_terms.تُبْ: repent; a command to return to Allah from wrongful possession
key_terms.حَقَّ: right; a rightful claim, which is negated here
key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: the way of Allah; the divine cause in which those slain are described as truly alive
key_terms.شَهِيدًا: a martyr; describing the death of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kāfī say about the Prophet’s martyrdom and the Imamate of ʿAlī and the eleven Imams?
ai.summary: This narration invokes the Qur'anic affirmation that those slain in the way of Allah are alive with their Lord, then applies that meaning to the martyrdom of the Prophet Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله). It further presents a declaration concerning the authority of ʿAlī (عليه السلام) and eleven from his descendants, alongside a call to repentance regarding usurped authority.

en.hubeali: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said to Abu Bakr one day:
‘[3:169] And reckon not those who are killed in Allah's Way as dead; but, they are alive (and) are being provided sustenance from their Lord.

And I<sup>asws</sup> testify that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> died as a martyr. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! He<sup>saww</sup> would be coming to you, therefore be convinced when he<sup>saww</sup> does come to you for the Satan<sup>la</sup> cannot be dreamt as being him<sup>saww</sup>’.

Ali<sup>asws</sup> grabbed Abu Bakr by the hand and showed him the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘O Abu Bakr! Believe in Ali<sup>asws</sup> and in eleven from his<sup>asws</sup> sons<sup>asws</sup>. They<sup>asws</sup> are like me<sup>saww</sup> except for the Prophet-hood, and repent to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from what is in your hands, for there isn’t a right for you in it’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>saww</sup> went as was not seen (again)’.
en.sarwar: 13. Through the same chain of narrators the following is narrated.
“Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) one day said to abu Bakr, “Do not think of those slain for the cause of God as dead.
They are alive with their Lord and receive sustenance from Him.”
[3:169].I testify that Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah died as a martyr. He by Allah, comes to you and do have any doubts when he will come to you. Satan can not appear in his disguise.”

Ali (a.s.) took the hand of abu Bakr and showed the Holy Prophet (s.a) to him who said to him, “O abu Bakr, believe in Ali and in the eleven Imams from his descendants. They are all like me except prophet-hood. Repent before Allah because of what you involvement in what you are involved. You have no right in it.”
The narrator has said that then he went and was not seen around.”
